correctness.rationale: With x=|U1|, the support of the intersection in each oriented direction is attained at an admissible disk support point, or else at a circle intersection: an interior point of just one smooth boundary arc can be a maximizer only at that disk's support point. The disk-admissibility tests are x≤−b or x≥a on the positive side and x≥b for the small-disk opposite support. The opposite large-disk support is impossible. The chord height identities give a≥|b|, hence the four branches in Eq. (1); a=b only for equal radii, and the zero-length cases and inclusive joins agree. The middle branch derivative is −rb−Hx/sqrt(1−x²), negative in the open branch and zero at its left end for b≤0. Thus the only plateau is at 2r for b<0 and the arcsine law of x gives its probability and linear onset. Solving the monotone middle branch selects the stated square-root inverse; the lower and upper inverse branches agree at their junctions. At the low end the exact linear support stage yields (6). At the high end the decrease is Hx²+O(x⁴) for b>0, (r/2)x²+O(x⁴) at b=0, and r³(x+b)²/(2H²)+O((x+b)³) just off the left plateau when b<0. Multiplying the inverse expansion there by the x-density 2r/(πH) gives (8), treating the atom separately. The lower-tail coefficient fixes d and m then fixes R+r; a positive atom yields 2r=M, otherwise 2H=M and the two-circle triangle area identity determines (R−r)² uniquely. This includes b=0 and R=r and excludes tangencies/containment. A separate bounded replay directly evaluated supports in 720 directions in each of six cases and checked joins, inversion, endpoint coefficients and recovery.
